title: Folk striped shawl
subtitle: A rectangle in horizontal treble stripes across three DK colours, changing colour every four rows
excerpt: This rectangular shawl works in horizontal treble stripes across three colours of DK yarn, with a colour change every four rows. The finished piece measures approximately 190 cm wide by 60 cm deep. The stripe sequence builds a bold folk-textile look that works in any combination of three coordinating shades.
heroPrompt: A rectangular crochet shawl in three colours of DK yarn, deep red, warm cream, and forest green, folded loosely on a wooden surface, showing clear horizontal stripe bands, photographed in natural light.

glossaryTerms.definition: To change colour on a treble stitch, work the final yarn-over pull-through of the last stitch of the old colour using the new colour, so the new colour appears at the top of that stitch and is ready for the turning chain.
Carrying an unused yarn up the side of the work by wrapping it around the working yarn at the start of each row, so you do not need to cut and rejoin it each time.

content.text: This rectangular shawl is worked flat from end to end in rows of treble, with the colour changing every four rows across three shades of DK yarn. The stripe sequence repeats throughout: four rows in colour A, four rows in colour B, four rows in colour C, then back to colour A. At 190 cm wide and 60 cm deep the finished piece wraps across the shoulders with plenty of length to drape, knot, or tuck.
The construction is rectangular. There is no shaping at any point. The only technique to manage is the
colour change in treble
at the end of every fourth row. The unused colours are carried up the selvedge using
float management
. This means you do not need to cut and rejoin at every stripe.

attrs.title: Materials
attrs.body: Approximately 200 g each of three colours of DK-weight yarn (600 g total). A 4 mm crochet hook (US G/6). Tapestry needle. Craft scissors. Blocking mat and pins. Tape measure.

content.text: Gauge

17 tr x 9 rows = 10 x 10 cm in DK yarn with a 4 mm hook, measured unstretched. Work a 15 x 15 cm swatch in treble, measure the central 10 x 10 cm area, and adjust hook size before beginning the shawl. Each extra stitch per 10 cm shifts the finished width by about 11 cm, so accurate tension here matters.
Stitches used
chain (ch): UK and US shared.
slip stitch (sl st): UK and US shared.
treble (tr): UK; the same move as US "double crochet" (dc).
Pattern

The shawl is worked flat from one short end to the other. Colour A is the first colour, B is the second, C is the third. The stripe sequence is 4 rows A, 4 rows B, 4 rows C, repeated throughout. Do not cut yarn at each colour change; instead carry the unused colours up the right-hand selvedge.
Foundation chain
Using colour A, ch 109. (This gives 108 working stitches and measures approximately 64 cm, which becomes the 60 cm depth after the body is worked and blocked.)
Row 1 (right side, colour A)
Ch 3 (counts as first tr throughout). 1 tr in each ch across. Turn. (108 sts)
Rows 2 to 4 (colour A)
Ch 3 (counts as first tr). 1 tr in each st across to end. Turn. (108 sts each row)
Colour change at row 5

At the end of row 4, work the last tr of colour A until 2 loops remain on hook, then draw colour B through both loops to complete the stitch. Drop colour A at the selvedge (do not cut). Continue with colour B.
Rows 5 to 8 (colour B)
Ch 3 (counts as first tr). 1 tr in each st across. Turn. (108 sts each row). At the end of row 8, change to colour C using the same method.
Rows 9 to 12 (colour C)
Ch 3 (counts as first tr). 1 tr in each st across. Turn. (108 sts each row). At the end of row 12, change back to colour A.
Continue to row 54

Repeat the 12-row stripe sequence (4 rows A, 4 rows B, 4 rows C) four more times, giving 54 rows in total. The shawl body measures approximately 190 cm wide at this point. On the final row, fasten off with colour C (or whichever colour completes a tidy final stripe).
Finishing

Fasten off and weave in all ends, including the carried floats up the selvedge. Work ends through the backs of stitches in the same colour stripe for at least 5 cm, changing direction once to secure. Wet-block by soaking in cool water for 10 minutes, pressing gently, then pinning to 190 x 60 cm on a blocking mat and leaving to dry completely.
Care
Handwash in cool water with mild soap. Do not tumble-dry. Lay flat on a clean towel and ease to shape while damp.
What to try next

Change the stripe width to 2 rows each for a narrower pinstripe effect, or 8 rows each for wider colour blocks. Working the same rectangle in double crochet (UK dc) on a smaller hook produces a denser, warmer fabric. A contrast-colour crochet border along all four edges gives a frame that ties the stripe colours together.
